questions.q: What input format does Prophet's fit() expect?
options: A NumPy array of values with no dates
A Series indexed by date, with the frequency set
A DataFrame with a date column named 'ds' and a numeric column named 'y'
A DataFrame with columns named 'date' and 'sales'
questions.explain: Prophet requires the columns to be named exactly ds (dates) and y (the value to forecast).

questions.q: Which set of components does Prophet combine to model a series?
options: Trend, seasonality (weekly and yearly), optional holidays, plus noise
Autoregressive terms, differencing and moving-average terms
Lagged features and a random forest
Only a level and a smoothing factor
questions.explain: Prophet is a decomposable model: a flexible trend, seasonal patterns, holiday effects, and an error term.

questions.q: In the lesson, the default Prophet scored an MAE of 24.2, but adding yearly_seasonality=True gave 6.71. What explains the difference?
options: Prophet cannot forecast without a yearly setting
The training history was just under two years, so the 'auto' setting left yearly seasonality off
yearly_seasonality=True changes the test data
The default model was trained on fewer days
questions.explain: By default Prophet enables yearly seasonality only for histories of at least two years. Printing m.seasonalities showed only 'weekly' was fitted.

questions.q: What do the initial, period and horizon arguments mean in Prophet's cross_validation()?
options: Horizon is the training length, initial is the forecast length
Period is the season length used for seasonality
All three set the number of Fourier terms
Initial is the first training window, period is the spacing between cutoffs, and horizon is how far each forecast reaches
questions.explain: cross_validation is a rolling-origin backtest: train on the initial window, forecast the horizon, then move the cutoff forward by the period and repeat.

questions.q: Why did adding US holidays not meaningfully improve the lesson's forecast?
options: Prophet ignores holiday inputs
US holidays cannot be used with daily data
The synthetic series had no holiday effects built in, so there was nothing for the holiday terms to learn
Holidays only work with cross_validation
questions.explain: Holiday terms help only when real holiday spikes or dips exist in the data. Here the tiny MAE change was noise.
